summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of kidney transplant rejection was readmitted two days after discharge due to nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and hyperkalemia with a potassium of 7.0. He had completed a dialysis session the prior day but developed symptoms later that evening. In the emergency department, he received insulin, dextrose, kayexalate, and ondansetron. Abdominal imaging showed air-fluid levels in the colon without obstruction or free air, consistent with mild viral gastroenteritis. He underwent hemodialysis on hospital day one, which normalized his potassium to 4.9. His gastrointestinal symptoms resolved, and he remained stable without chest pain or respiratory issues. He was discharged home in good condition with no medication changes and instructions to resume normal activities and follow-up care.
